previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and a history of bladder cancer with ileal conduit was admitted for a urinary tract infection with multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus, presenting with nausea, vomiting with blood, melena, and recurrent falls. He developed hypotension and bleeding from ileal conduit varices, requiring transfusion and transfer to the MICU. A TIPS procedure with sclerotherapy successfully reduced portal pressure and stopped the bleeding. He experienced transient hepatic encephalopathy post-procedure, managed with lactulose and rifaximine. An ileus resolved during admission. The patient completed a 10-day course of IV antibiotics and was clinically stable but left against medical advice before formal discharge. He returned the next day for PICC removal and prescriptions, with instructions to continue liver-directed therapies and follow up with specialists.

EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ status post TIPS procedure who presents with abdominal pain
and rectal bleeding, evaluate for TIPS patency.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler ultrasound images of the
abdomen were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Prior TIPS ultrasound dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

The liver appears diffusely coarsened and nodular consistent with known
cirrhosis.  No focal liver lesions are identified. There is small volume
perihepatic ascites. There is borderline splenomegaly, with the spleen
measuring 13.0 cm.  There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CHD
measures 3 mm. There is no evidence of stones or gallbladder wall thickening.

The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.
The TIPS is patent and demonstrates wall-to-wall flow.
Portal vein and intra-TIPS velocities are as follows:
Main portal vein: 34 cm/sec, previously 90 cm/sec
Proximal TIPS: 95 cm/sec, previously 89cm/sec
Mid TIPS: 156 cm/sec, previously 206 cm/sec
Distal TIPS: 215  cm/sec, previously 200 cm/sec

Flow within the left portal vein is towards the TIPS shunt.

PANCREAS: The imaged portion of the pancreas appears within normal limits,
without masses or pancreatic ductal dilation, with portions of the pancreatic
tail obscured by overlying bowel gas.

KIDNEYS:  Limited views of the kidneys demonstrate no hydronephrosis.


RETROPERITONEUM: Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. Patent TIPS with unchanged intra TIPS velocities.
2. Cirrhotic liver with borderline splenomegaly and new trace ascites.
